nodes.name: PDF Inspector
nodes.summary: Native PDF inspection component that extracts selectable text, layout, tables, and page geometry without OCR.

nodes.name: Docling
nodes.summary: Document conversion library used for non-OCR normalization of supported native document formats.

nodes.name: GLM-OCR
nodes.summary: Local OCR engine that owns recognized layout and geometry for scanned visual documents.

nodes.name: PaddleOCR-VL
nodes.summary: Local OCR engine that can own layout, recognition, confidence, and reading order for scanned documents.

nodes.name: Visual recovery
nodes.summary: Optional bounded OCR recovery mechanism that can replace text within existing recognized elements.

nodes.name: Deterministic manifests retain Docling provenance
nodes.summary: Docling conversion is grounded by claiming converted records against deterministic, format-specific source manifests rather than treating converted output as the source of truth.

nodes.name: Mixed-PDF page routes require confirmation
nodes.summary: PDF Inspector may suggest native or OCR page routes, but users confirm or override every route and failures remain on the selected route.

nodes.name: Unusable native pages require Mixed PDF
nodes.summary: A native-PDF run stops and recommends Mixed PDF when inspection finds unusable pages instead of silently rasterizing or invoking OCR.

nodes.name: Visual recovery preserves OCR geometry
nodes.summary: Optional visual recovery may only replace text within existing elements; it cannot create, delete, reorder, or alter their geometry or types.

nodes.name: Embedded native-document media is recorded, not OCRed
nodes.summary: Embedded media becomes recorded assets while native source units remain structural elements such as paragraphs, shapes, cells, tables, rows, and columns.

nodes.name: Scanned processing excludes native PDF inspection
nodes.summary: The scanned-PDF and image mode does not invoke native PDF inspection, preserving existing OCR provider selection and recovery semantics.

nodes.name: Accepted native values require exact evidence
nodes.summary: An accepted value must exactly match immutable base text, have complete character-span coverage, and resolve to a source anchor; rendered Markdown is not extraction input.

nodes.name: Manual selection controls exactly one pipeline
nodes.summary: Each file has an independent authoritative processing selection, validated against signatures and containers, which reaches exactly one top-level pipeline with no automatic reinterpretation.

nodes.name: Native libraries do not perform OCR
nodes.summary: The first native release excludes OCR inside PDF Inspector, Docling, and LangExtract to protect source traceability.

edges.description: The article describes Docling as the normalized converter constrained by deterministic source manifests.
The native PDF workflow uses PDF Inspector for non-OCR text, layout, tables, and geometry extraction.
PDF Inspector supplies the suggested native-or-OCR page routes in mixed documents.
GLM-OCR is named as an OCR engine that owns scanned-document recognition and geometry.
PaddleOCR-VL is named as an OCR engine that owns scanned-document recognition and geometry.
The article specifies the bounds of optional visual recovery.
Mixed-page review implements the product rule that user-selected routes are authoritative.
Native PDF stopping on unusable pages applies the no-silent-rerouting requirement.
Docling record claiming applies the product evidence contract to converted native content.
The recovery boundary is the OCR counterpart to evidence ownership and traceability.
The format pipeline implements the declared scope and the no-OCR embedded-media boundary.
The system overview identifies evidence ownership as the central product boundary.
